conclusion: Megatron PR #4839 is not needed for the current Miles DeepSeek-V4 path because Miles implements its own HC and the HC math matches the fixed H_res.T formula. The QAT dimension and official-compatible in-place QAT fixes are applied, and operator, attention-module, attention-trace replay, MLP expert replay, grouped-MLP training math, EP=8 all-to-all dispatch math, and transformer-block training-step gates now pass. Full mini-checkpoint forward and SFT one-step execute with finite values. Mini forward and SFT one-step routing replay show that MoE routing flips are a major drift amplifier. Mini activation replay proves that once dense layer outputs or final layernorm output are injected, sparse/tilelang reproduce dense logprobs bitwise, ruling out final layernorm/output-head/logprob postprocessing as the remaining backend drift source. Mini sublayer replay further shows that injecting all dense attention outputs alone is sufficient for bitwise dense logprobs, while injecting all dense MLP outputs is not, localizing remaining backend drift to attention module output differences. Mini attention-layer replay shows layer 0 attention is the largest early contributor and attention-prefix injection monotonically reduces mismatches to zero. Mini attention I/O replay confirms that this is same-input attention backend BF16 output drift, not merely upstream input-state drift. Mini attention I/O local training-step replay passes on real checkpoint attention inputs and proves the attention forward/backward/manual-update surface remains within BF16 training thresholds. Complete SFT one-step with attention-output straight-through replay also passes after removing the localized attention forward-value drift, with exact loss parity and selected update drift below threshold. A dedicated mini checkpoint correctness gate now passes under the declared BF16 training tolerance by composing the loaded 4-layer checkpoint SFT rerun, an explicit PyTorch SFT loss reference, routed MoE math, EP=8 dispatch math, attention I/O training-step bounds, c0/c4/c128 external attention references, optimizer math, and the BF16 envelope. The external training-reference 1-layer gate now passes for non-compressed attention, compress_ratio=4 indexer attention, deterministic compress_ratio=128 compressed attention, and a score-routed MoE/shared-expert block: an explicit PyTorch formula reference matches Megatron/Miles on forward, loss, input gradient, selected parameter gradients, and one SGD update within each path's declared thresholds; the MoE block reference separately covers sqrtsoftplus top-k routing, shared expert, grouped routed experts, and one SGD update under BF16 MoE tolerance. However real non-injected SFT loss and forward logprob strict parity still fail without activation injection, so the result is a BF16-tolerant mini-checkpoint training correctness proof, not a strict bitwise/full-logprob proof. A proof ledger consistency check now machine-validates the artifact chain and found no failures. An explicit end-to-end BF16 tolerance verifier now passes and documents the bounded real-forward/train-step drift envelope without reclassifying strict parity as passed. A dedicated official-vs-Miles BF16 forward tolerance verifier also passes and records the official-inference strict parity boundary. Optimizer path and AdamW first-step update math are now verified as a separate PASS gate. Source regression guards for the precision fixes are now verified and included in the proof ledger. A proof coverage matrix now maps the user-requested proof areas to artifact-backed evidence and machine-checks the remaining strict gates as explicit boundaries. Environment provenance is now machine-checked against the operator-math runtime artifact. External reference provenance now records the bounded use of Megatron-LM PR #4839 and SWIFT documentation.

not_proved.reason: with deterministic runtime enabled, strict rtol=0.002, atol=0.02 pairwise logprob comparisons still fail. Routing replay separates the discrete MoE assignment flip from continuous drift: dense-vs-sparse improves from 205/402 mismatches, max_abs=0.5140819549560547, mean_abs=0.07136902213096619, relative_l2_gap=1.547721555139603e-05 to 84/402 mismatches, max_abs=0.255859375, mean_abs=0.030136708170175552, relative_l2_gap=3.5204090861329362e-06; dense-vs-tilelang improves from 200/402 to 75/402; sparse-vs-tilelang improves from 201/402 to 59/402. Activation replay further proves the post-layer path: injecting dense layer 0..3 outputs or dense final_layernorm output into sparse/tilelang produces bitwise-exact dense logprobs, while injecting only earlier prefixes reduces but does not eliminate drift. Sublayer replay localizes the remaining backend drift to attention module outputs: injecting all dense attention outputs makes sparse/tilelang bitwise exact, while injecting all dense MLP outputs does not. Layerwise attention replay shows layer 0 attention is the largest early contributor, and attention-prefix injection monotonically reduces mismatches to zero. Attention I/O replay then removes input-state drift from the comparison: even with dense attention inputs replayed, sparse/tilelang attention outputs differ from dense by at most 0.0625 and layer 0 has the largest mean_abs. Therefore MLP, HC, final layernorm, output head, and logprob code are not the source once attention outputs are identical; strict mini forward remains unproved because the real non-injected attention backend path still has BF16 output drift. The proof ledger machine-checks this localization chain: routing replay reduces all pairwise relative_l2 gaps by 4.39x-6.37x, all-attention activation replay restores dense logprobs bitwise for sparse/tilelang while MLP-only replay does not, and attention I/O replay bounds same-input attention output drift at <= 0.0625. Under the explicit BF16 tolerance envelope, the real non-injected backend forward remains bounded: all pairwise relative_l2 gaps are <= 2e-05, mean_abs <= 0.08, and p99_abs <= 0.37.

same-environment QAT/0415 train-step execution is finite, and selected_grad_max_rel_gap plus selected_state_max_abs pass their strict thresholds for dense-vs-sparse, dense-vs-tilelang, and sparse-vs-tilelang. However real non-injected loss_abs_global_max still fails: without routing replay the gaps are 1.5947265625, 0.703125, and 0.8916015625; with dense routing replay they improve to 1.1494140625, 0.5341796875, and 0.615234375, still far above max_loss_abs=0.02. A separate attention I/O local training-step replay on real mini-checkpoint attention inputs passes: output max_abs <= 0.0625, input_grad max_abs <= 9.5367431640625e-07, relative gaps <= 2.8061398839485108e-05, and manual SGD state_after_step max_abs == 0.0 across dense/sparse/tilelang. Complete SFT one-step with dense routing replay plus attention-output straight-through replay also passes: loss_abs_global_max=0.0, selected_grad_max_rel_gap <= 2.1433698600525908e-05, and selected_state_max_abs=4.76837158203125e-07. This proves the complete training chain after the already-localized attention forward-value drift is removed, but the strict gate remains open for the real non-injected forward because complete SFT loss still amplifies accumulated BF16 forward drift. The proof ledger machine-checks that the complete SFT attention-output straight-through replay has exact loss parity and selected gradient/update bounds, so the open strict gate is specifically the real non-injected forward path. Under the same BF16 tolerance envelope, real non-injected selected_grad_max_rel_gap is <= 5e-04 and selected_state_max_abs is <= 2e-05; after attention-output replay, complete SFT loss parity is exact. Optimizer update math is separately verified: the DeepSeek-V4 runner uses Adam hyperparameters, Miles train step calls Megatron optimizer.step(), and first-step AdamW selected-update math has a worst-case adaptive update disagreement of about 2e-06, below the selected-state threshold.

after QAT fixes, 1-layer BF16 official-vs-Miles sparse improves to 63/402 mismatches, max_abs=0.16042709350585938, mean_abs=0.03158159181475639, relative_l2_gap=2.313715897095392e-06; tilelang is same order with 71/402 mismatches and relative_l2_gap=2.4187967853084302e-06. Attention trace replay passes. Loaded weight mapping now covers embedding, attention, pre-MLP layernorm, router, hash tid2eid, shared experts, all 256 routed expert fc1/fc2 tensors, final layernorm, and output layer with exact_equal=True and nonzero_abs_count=0. MLP trace compare shows layer-0 hash router expert indices are exact_equal, router selected weights have 0 mismatches, and shared experts have 0 mismatches, while routed expert aggregation still drifts. MLP expert replay proves official routed expert formula plus shared expert exactly reproduces official ffn output, and Megatron BF16 activation replay is closer to Miles MLP output than official FP32 activation replay, so the remaining MLP difference is localized past routing indices and both Miles/official weight conversion. Grouped MLP math verification proves local TEGroupedMLP forward/backward/update is bitwise exact against an explicit per-expert BF16 formula at production hidden/FFN dimensions, so the remaining full-forward drift is not explained by a local TEGroupedMLP GEMM/SwiGLU/probability-application formula error. Runtime precision variants show strict drift is sensitive to official FP32-vs-Megatron-like BF16 execution choices: the all-BF16 variant reduces sparse mismatches from 63 to 53 and mean_abs from 0.03158159181475639 to 0.023050455376505852, although strict parity still fails. Head replay proves official saved logprobs are exact from official final hidden + FP32 head, while Miles saved logprobs are replayed by Miles final hidden + BF16 head matmul with 0 mismatches and max_abs=1.9073486328125e-06. The remaining strict logprob failure therefore contains full MoE training-runtime/final-hidden drift plus FP32-vs-BF16 output head precision drift, and is past the verified attention-core/local-expert/math gates. The official forward BF16 tolerance verifier checks the 1-layer official-vs-Miles sparse/tilelang drift against relative_l2_gap <= 5e-06, mean_abs <= 0.04, p99_abs <= 0.15, and max_abs <= 0.20, while preserving the fact that strict rtol/atol parity still fails. Source regression guards now confirm the QAT and compressor fixes remain present, so the remaining official-vs-Miles strict drift is not due to reverting those known precision fixes.

layer 0/1/2 router assignment maps are exact-equal, but layer 3 router assignment differs and routed experts shape changes; routing replay removes the discrete layerwise routing mismatch and reduces full mini-forward backend logprob drift by about 4-7x in relative_l2_gap. Independent EP=8 all-to-all dispatch math passes bitwise for forward/backward/update, including an empty receiving expert and top-3 multi-route. Activation replay shows that after dense layer 0..3 outputs or dense final_layernorm output are injected, sparse and tilelang reproduce dense logprobs bitwise; therefore the post-transformer output path is ruled out for backend drift. Sublayer replay shows all dense attention outputs are sufficient to recover bitwise dense logprobs, while all dense MLP outputs are not. Layerwise attention replay shows the attention drift is cumulative: injecting layer 0 alone strongly reduces mismatches, injecting later single attention layers is insufficient, and injecting attention prefixes monotonically reaches bitwise exact at layer 0..3. Attention I/O replay confirms the drift remains when attention inputs are replayed from dense, with all attention output max_abs <= 0.0625 and finite. Attention I/O local training-step replay further proves that on the same real checkpoint attention inputs, dense/sparse/tilelang input gradients and manual SGD updates remain within threshold. Complete SFT one-step with attention-output straight-through replay passes after removing the localized attention forward-value drift, proving the remaining train-step chain. Strict full mini-forward parity still fails without activation injection, so the remaining production MoE path issue is localized to accumulated continuous BF16 attention-output drift inside transformer layers and real router amplification, not to a standalone all-to-all dispatcher formula error.

the mini checkpoint correctness gate now passes under the declared BF16 training tolerance and covers loaded 4-layer checkpoint execution, explicit PyTorch SFT loss reference, routed MoE evidence, a score-routed MoE/shared-expert one-layer external reference, SFT loss replay, attention I/O training-step bounds, and optimizer math through composed artifacts. What remains missing is a single monolithic external training reference written in PyTorch that reimplements the full 4-layer checkpoint, EP=8 routed MoE, SFT loss, backward, and update end to end; this is still MISSING_INPUT and not a new training-link failure.
